**Adjacency note for the planner — #2052 touches the same watcher surface. Read before editing `autonomous_session_watch.py`.**

`#2052` ("keep-running shields provably-idle pods when owner is alive") and this task both loosen the `keep-running` shield in the pod-safety pass. They are DISTINCT and complementary, but they edit neighbouring code and must not be planned in isolation.

**#2052** — pod HAS a runtime and is provably idle (GPU 0%, no workload processes, empty `/workspace/logs/`). Signal: `pod_audit.py`'s `idle_gpu`. Action: ESCALATE (alert), never a stop. Driving incident: two duplicate `pod-1739` pods billing ~$187 over 29.4 h and 15.8 h while idle.

**This task (#2060)** — pod NEVER obtained a runtime at all (`runtime: null`, no port-22 mapping since creation). Action: TERMINATE, plus a provision-side teardown so the leak never reaches the watcher in the first place.

**Why #2052's fix would NOT have caught this incident.** Its signal is GPU idleness read from the pod. On `pod-1947-loc` there was no SSH endpoint at all, so `pod_audit` could not reach the box to compute `idle_gpu` — the pod is unreachable BY DEFINITION of the failure. The two arms therefore key on genuinely different observables: one on "reachable but doing nothing", the other on "never became reachable". Neither subsumes the other.

**Planning guidance.** Keep the two carve-outs separately named and separately gated (distinct env knobs, distinct sidecar reasons) rather than merging them into one predicate — they differ in action (escalate vs terminate) and in evidentiary strength. The never-ran case supports outright termination because a pod that never exposed a runtime provably holds no work; the idle-but-reachable case is weaker and correctly stops at escalation. Merging them risks either over-reaping a live-but-quiet pod or under-reaping a dead one.

If #2052 lands first, this task's watcher half should slot alongside its arm rather than rewriting it. If this one lands first, the same in reverse. Coordinate on the shared file; do not let two sessions edit `decide_pod_safety_action` / the keep-running arms concurrently — concurrent same-file workflow edits on this repo have already cost real time tonight (see #2055, the SLURM lane-collision filing from the same session).

Also adjacent, lower overlap: `#2011` (provisioner avoids a known-bad RunPod host on retry) — relevant to this task's retry path, since the driving incident here is a bad host, but it does not touch the billing-leak predicate.

**Third facet of this defect, from the live post-mortem — the fallback chain dead-ends on its own wedged residue.**

The owning agent's account of `pod-1947-loc`, which completes the failure picture in the task body:

> "the provision fallback chain's 4xH100 rung created the pod, its own bootstrap wait exited without ever seeing SSH (RUNNING-but-no-port host wedge), and the chain's later rungs refused on 'pod already exists', so nothing was driving it."

So the leak is not only "provision exits without teardown" (facet a) and "keep-running blocks the reaper" (facet b). There is a third, and it is arguably the most damaging because it converts a recoverable capacity fallback into a silent dead-end:

**(c) A capacity-fallback chain's later rungs refuse on "pod already exists" when the existing pod is the WEDGED residue of an earlier rung.** The name-collision guard cannot distinguish "a healthy pod for this issue already exists, do not double-provision" from "an earlier rung of THIS SAME chain left a dead pod behind". So the chain stops advancing, no rung ever produces a usable pod, and the wedged one keeps billing. All three facets have to hold for the leak to persist, and on this incident all three did.

**The correct behaviour has now been demonstrated live.** The manual retry chain built in response terminates the residue BETWEEN rungs and only then advances: RETRY 1 (4x H100) failed to bootstrap, its pod was terminated, RETRY 2 (4x H200) provisioned cleanly and exposed SSH within ~37 s. That inter-rung teardown is exactly what the built-in fallback chain lacks, and it also bounds each wedge's billing to one bootstrap-wait window (~15 min) instead of unbounded.

**Planning guidance.** Treat (c) as in scope for this task rather than a separate filing — it is the same money leak and the same code neighbourhood, and fixing (a) largely implies it: if a rung tears down the pod it created when bootstrap fails, the next rung no longer sees a stale "pod already exists" and advances naturally. But make it explicit in the plan, because a narrow (a) that only fires on the FINAL rung's failure, or that leaves the name registered, would not close it. The chain also needs a bounded stop: after N failed rungs it should terminate the residue and fail loud rather than spin — the manual chain used N=2 followed by ALL_RETRIES_FAILED and a fall back to the free SLURM lane, which is a reasonable shape to copy.

Cost of this incident: roughly 25 minutes of 4x H100 billing on the wedged pod before a human noticed and asked.
